A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 12 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a complete comparison; changes are confined to the first-page header.

before.justification: v1 reports original entropy/tool-quality pilot experiments in Table 1 and TEPO benchmark evaluations in Tables 2–4, alongside further empirical analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original pilot experiments, TEPO benchmark results, and supplementary empirical analyses reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same TEPO sparse and dense reward designs, token-level GRPO objective, and advantage-assignment procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data and eight evaluation datasets across mathematical reasoning, multi-hop QA, and deep search. The wiki-18 retrieval setting and GAIA evaluation using Bing are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–4 is unchanged, including GRPO, ARPO, AEPO, SearchR1-PPO, OTC-GRPO, OTC-PPO, and StepSearch. The baseline comparisons in Figure 3 also match.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B retain the same model configurations, training budgets, evaluation procedures, metrics, and dataset subsets, including the first 500 HLE questions.

E4.justification: The model-scaling, training-dynamics, and entropy/tool-quality analyses in Section 5 are identical. Appendix C retains the same failed-call analysis and Figure 7.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five evaluation runs and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Section 4.3. The five independent pilot trials in Appendix A.3 and uncertainty reporting in the tables are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, rankings, and trends match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 reports the same Qwen2.5 TEPOdense average accuracy of 42.39 and average tool-call count of 3.99 in both versions.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain identical formal definitions and equations for tool interaction, entropy, rewards, and advantages. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same entropy-supervision contribution and the same claims about sparse rewards improving efficiency and dense rewards improving performance.

C2.justification: The efficiency/performance explanations, HLE retrieval interpretation, and failed-query discussion are unchanged. Both versions state the same limitations concerning larger models and broader testing of real-time search APIs.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain identical judge prompts, training-data details, hyperparameters, four-H200 hardware setup, and inference settings. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the references are identical, including the positioning of TEPO against earlier methods that use entropy for exploration rather than rewarding entropy-reducing tool calls.

P1.justification: The first-page author block removes Mengdi Wang and the Princeton affiliation, adds Haven, and updates Zhenfei Yin's affiliations. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; body wording and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: v3 adds five institutional logos and a horizontal rule above the title. All numbered figures, tables, and captions are unchanged, and pages 2–12 render identically.

improvement.justification: The revisions concern author/affiliation information and a decorative header. Methods, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility details—including Appendices A–C—are unchanged, providing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
